spec.topic: The Killing Ledger — Keddie cabin murders (1981), host-led true-crime documentary

assignedLines.text: April 1981. In a tiny California mountain cabin, three people were murdered — while three children slept through it all in the next room.
assignedLines.camera: slow push-in, wide to medium close-up; grave, cold intensity

assignedLines.text: This is Cabin 28, in the resort town of Keddie. What happened here that night is one of America's most disturbing unsolved crimes.
assignedLines.camera: lateral dolly left-to-right at eye level; somber, measured

assignedLines.text: Sue Sharp, a 36-year-old mother, had moved her five children here just months earlier — chasing a quieter, safer life.
assignedLines.camera: static medium shot, subtle breathing drift; soft, melancholic

assignedLines.text: On the evening of April 11th, everything looked normal. Kids were home. The night was cold, quiet — ordinary in every way.
assignedLines.camera: low-angle crane-up settling to eye level; calm with unease underneath

assignedLines.text: Fourteen-year-old Sheila had gone to a friend's cabin for the night. That one ordinary decision would save her life.
assignedLines.camera: handheld drift circling right, then settle front-center; quiet gravity

assignedLines.text: Sue's 15-year-old son John and his 17-year-old friend Dana Wingate were expected back home that evening. They never came back.
assignedLines.camera: slow pull-back revealing wider frame; heavy, foreboding
